topic: B2B Partner Ecosystems and Channel Strategy
headline: Has Your Partner Demand Strategy Kept Up With Your Evolving Partner Ecosystem?
keyNotes: It's surprising that many companies still use a single, old-fashioned marketing plan for all their business partners, even though these partners are very diverse. This leads to wasted money, unhappy partners, and poor results.

A big change is coming: 70% of leaders responsible for marketing with business partners plan to update their marketing plans for these partners within the next year. This shows many realize their current approach isn't working.

The article highlights that a marketing plan designed for one type of business partner can actually be ineffective or even harmful when applied to another. This is because different partners create value and reach customers in very different ways.

Simply adding more money or programs won't fix the problem; instead, companies need to create specific marketing plans that are carefully matched to how each business partner creates value and sells products.
question: The article emphasizes that a "one-size-fits-all" approach to working with partners often fails because each partner is unique. Where in your own work or relationships do you currently use a single approach for different situations, and how might tailoring your strategy to each specific case lead to better outcomes?
